questions.question: What is biological evolution?
choices: A change in one organism's habits during life
A change in inherited population characteristics across generations
An increase in an individual's body size
A daily change in local weather

questions.question: What is natural selection?
choices: Differential reproductive success associated with heritable traits
The deliberate choice of mates by scientists only
A process in which organisms request useful mutations
The inheritance of every acquired behavior

questions.question: What is an adaptation in evolutionary biology?
choices: Any injury sustained during an organism's life
Any temporary change in an organism's mood
A trait guaranteed to help in every environment
A heritable feature that improves success in a particular environment

questions.question: What can produce new alleles in a population?
choices: Exercise
Seasonal migration
Mutation
Competition alone

questions.question: What does fitness refer to in evolutionary biology?
choices: Freedom from all disease
Physical strength in every setting
An individual's maximum running speed
Reproductive contribution to later generations

questions.question: Which process involves humans choosing organisms with desired traits to reproduce?
choices: Genetic drift
Artificial selection
Natural selection
Gene flow

questions.question: What is a fossil?
choices: Preserved remains or traces of past life
A modern reconstruction based on ancient remains
Any living organism that is very old
A rock containing no evidence of an organism

questions.question: Why must a trait be heritable for selection on that trait to drive evolutionary change?
choices: All inherited traits are equally beneficial
Acquired injuries always alter gamete DNA
The trait's effects must be passed into later generations
Selection acts only on traits absent from parents

questions.question: Why do populations, rather than individual organisms, evolve through natural selection?
choices: Evolution requires every individual to change in the same way
Each organism deliberately rewrites its genes as needed
Inherited trait frequencies change as generations replace one another
Individuals never vary in inherited traits

questions.question: How can similar underlying limb structures in different vertebrates support evolution?
choices: They prove the animals have identical diets
They exclude any role for inheritance
They show every vertebrate evolved at the same time
They can provide evidence of common ancestry

questions.question: Why can a trait beneficial in one habitat be less useful in another?
choices: Mutation stops whenever habitats differ
The trait's effects depend on environmental conditions
All habitats impose identical survival demands
A beneficial trait must always increase body size

questions.question: What is genetic drift?
choices: Random changes in allele frequencies, especially influential in small populations
The formation of alleles because organisms need them
The planned movement of animals between parks
The directed copying of only dominant genes

questions.question: How does gene flow affect populations?
choices: Movement and reproduction can transfer alleles between populations
It requires every individual to have the same genotype
It changes rocks into fossils
It prevents all inherited variation

questions.question: Why does antibiotic use select for resistant bacteria?
choices: Antibiotics intentionally produce the same helpful mutation in every bacterium
Bacteria stop reproducing when resistance develops
Resistant bacteria may survive treatment and reproduce more successfully
Resistance is always caused by a patient's behavior

questions.question: Why is scientific evidence for evolution drawn from multiple fields?
choices: Only fossils can provide useful evidence
Different fields must always produce unrelated conclusions
DNA comparisons are unrelated to ancestry
Fossils, anatomy, genetics, and other evidence can test related explanations

questions.question: Dark beetles are harder for predators to see on dark bark, and color is inherited. What may happen over generations?
choices: Every beetle immediately changes color
Dark coloration may become more frequent
Light beetles stop passing any alleles to offspring
Predators cause a directed mutation in every beetle

questions.question: A storm randomly kills most members of a small population, regardless of their traits. Which process most directly fits a resulting allele-frequency change?
choices: Acquired inheritance
Artificial selection
Directed mutation
Genetic drift

questions.question: A student says giraffes inherited longer necks because their parents stretched to reach leaves. What is the better natural-selection explanation?
choices: Inherited neck-length variation affected survival and reproduction over generations
Stretching changed every parent's gamete DNA
Every giraffe developed the same neck length in one generation
Food availability prevented hereditary differences

questions.question: A population's environment changes. Which information best helps predict selection?
choices: The average age of individuals without considering reproduction
Which traits occur only because of individual practice
How existing heritable variation affects reproductive success in the new conditions
Whether all inherited differences disappear when conditions change

questions.question: Two related populations become reproductively isolated over many generations. What evolutionary outcome may follow?
choices: Every mutation disappears
Formation of distinct species
All genetic differences are automatically reversed
Both populations must become identical
